title: Editorial vs Swiss Style
lede: Both are typographic, both use a single accent, both refuse decoration. They disagree about what a page should constrain: the reader's line, or the page's columns.
verdict: Editorial controls line length — a 17-character headline and a 46-character standfirst. Swiss controls column position — a headline across nine of twelve columns, with the standfirst starting at column seven, deliberately overlapping.
brief: These two are the closest pair in the gallery in spirit and the furthest apart in method. Editorial is a single column with hard limits on how wide any text may run; Swiss is a twelve-column grid where the interest comes from where blocks start and how far they span.

That means they fail differently. Editorial collapses when content refuses to be narrow — a wide table, a code block, a four-up card row. Swiss collapses when the grid is dropped at a narrow breakpoint and everything simply stacks, because the asymmetry was the only idea the layout had.

dimensions.name: Layout constraint
dimensions.a: Line length: 17ch headline, 46ch standfirst, 32ch card copy

dimensions.name: Accent
dimensions.a: One colour on links and rules
dimensions.b: One red, appearing twice on the page

dimensions.name: Density
dimensions.a: Generous vertical space, few elements per screen
dimensions.b: Tighter rows, more content above the fold

whenA: The page is read rather than scanned — an essay, a case study, a long product story
The content is text-first and there is little data to lay out
You want a warm, unhurried voice and the site has few competing elements
whenB: The page must carry several kinds of content on one screen — numbers, cards, a list, a quote
You want the layout itself to look designed without adding colour or decoration
The brand is institutional, technical or financial, where Helvetica reads as competence
promptDelta: Ask for a measure for editorial and column spans for Swiss — not the other way round. A model told to build an editorial page without a measure will produce the browser default of roughly 140 characters, and a model told to build Swiss without column spans will produce a single centred column that looks like a blog. Both styles are decided by one line of constraint, and it is a different line in each case.
